card.old: In my opinion, the most effective approach is a synthesis of both.
card.neu: → The most effective approach is, therefore, a synthesis of both.
card.note: Overusing 'In my opinion' and 'I believe' weakens academic writing. While expressing personal views is appropriate in IELTS essays, these phrases should appear sparingly (once, typically in the introduction or conclusion) rather than multiple times throughout the essay. Direct assertions with appropriate hedging ('therefore', 'thus', 'consequently') are more effective in academic contexts.
card.noteBlue: This pattern of overusing first-person hedging phrases is one of the most common style weaknesses among Chinese IELTS candidates and can limit scores to 7.0 in Lexical Resource and Coherence and Cohesion. Reducing these to one or two instances and replacing with logical connectors can elevate the score.
